_about: Known-item retrieval: the user pastes a registry id and wants that trial.
GROUND TRUTH IS EXACT AND INVOLVES NO JUDGEMENT. Every one of the 10,666 rows
carries a unique Trial ID, so the answer to 'NCT04372368' is defined, not judged.
That makes this the only stratum in the project with no annotator provenance to
declare -- and the reason it is a separate instrument from round 3's `code`
stratum, which asks a different question.
`code` scores 'which trials CITE this id', and its gold sets list citing trials
only -- excluding the queried trial itself by construction, not by judgement.
This stratum scores 'give me THIS trial'. Both are legitimate; they are not the
same task, and neither gold set answers the other's question.
Sampling: 5 ids per registry, all 12 registries, random.seed(0),
drawn from sorted ids so the fixture regenerates identically. Stratifying matters
because id shape varies by registry (CTRI/2021/05/033883 against NCT04912934
against 2021-001036-25) and normalisation has to survive all of them.
